question: This is the as-found single-line diagram of a building's 480 V switchgear. Utility 2 is out of service, so standby generator G1 is running and carries every load it is connected to through closed breakers. Then main breaker 52-M1 trips. The operator restores power with this procedure: (1) find the loads that were running before the trip and lost power; (2) tie breaker 52-T (now open) will be closed, which re-energizes only what can then be reached from G1 through closed breakers; (3) G1's rating is printed next to it on the drawing; if G1's total load after closing 52-T would exceed that rating, the operator first opens the load breakers of loads that 52-T would restore, one at a time, largest kW first, until the total is at or below the rating; (4) the operator closes 52-T. No other breaker changes position. A load behind an open breaker was not running before the trip. What is the total kW of the loads that were running before the trip and are not running at the end (loads shed in step 3 plus loads 52-T cannot reach)? Answer with an integer number of kW.
references: IEEE Std 141 (Red Book), secondary-selective / main-tie-main low-voltage switchgear single-line diagrams
IEEE Std 315 / ANSI Y32.2 graphic symbols and ANSI/IEEE C37.2 device numbers (52 = AC circuit breaker)
